title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes
abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for a one-dimensional $p$-$n$ junction diode, conditioned on device length, doping and bias. Using the internal state of the device as predicted by the surrogate we develop a test-suite of quantities of interest including the terminal current, depletion width, peak field and stored charge. The formalism and the quantities are can be extended to asymmetric junction and two-dimensional diodes as shown by means of benchmark analysis. For the one-dimensional symmetric junction surrogate, we obtain 0.11% median $L_1$ error on the electrostatic potential, and 1.5% and 0.61% on the electron and hole densities. Finally, we develop an uncertainty analysis which determines the validity of surrogate answer within the user-specified tolerance.
summary: This work develops a physics-informed, uncertainty-aware surrogate model using PINNs to rapidly simulate the complex electrical behavior of $p$-$n$ junction diodes. By embedding the underlying semiconductor physics into the neural network loss function, the model accurately predicts key quantities like current and electric fields. This significantly accelerates device simulation while providing rigorous estimates of prediction uncertainty.
main_problem: The goal is to create a fast, reliable, and uncertainty-aware surrogate model to replace computationally expensive Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations for $p$-$n$ junction diodes.
main_result: The developed physics-informed surrogate model achieves high accuracy for key observables like terminal current and depletion width, significantly outperforming data-only approaches.
method: The authors employ Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) trained on the coupled electrostatic and carrier-transport equations governing the diode.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a semiconductor $p$-$n$ junction diode, governed by drift-diffusion equations and Poisson's equation, formulated using the quasi-Fermi-level parametrization.
key_observables: Terminal current ($J$), depletion width ($W$), peak electric field ($E_{peak}$), and stored charges ($Q_n, Q_p$).
important_parameters: Device length, doping profile, and applied bias voltage.
main_assumptions: The model relies on the PINN framework to enforce physical laws, and the uncertainty analysis is crucial for determining the validity of predictions.
figures_summary: Figures compare error distributions and performance metrics for readout current ($\hat{J}_{RO}$) versus differentiated current ($\hat{J}_{grad}$) across varying device lengths and doping levels.
paper_structure: The paper details the formulation using PINNs, derives various quantities of interest (QoIs) from the network output, compares the readout current method against direct differentiation, and rigorously quantifies the error and uncertainty bounds.
why_interesting: While focused on semiconductor devices, the core methodology—using PINNs to embed complex, coupled partial differential equations into a machine learning framework—is a powerful general technique for modeling physical systems that could be adapted to quantum many-body or open quantum system dynamics.

The 2D planar benchmark device (contact thickness exaggerated): a p+ implant (nA = 1018 cm−3, 1.26 µm wide, 0.64 µm deep) in an n−substrate (nD = 1016 cm−3) of width 3 µm and height 2 µm. The anode is a window on the top face, the cathode covers the bottom face, and the remaining boundary is insulating.

Rows: potential (DEVSIM, solid black; network, dashed blue); electron (solid) and hole (dash-dot) densities; and the relative error of n, p and ψ (dashed line: 20%).

Figure 4. State of the 2D planar benchmark at the held-out voltage V = 0.44 V, on the trimmed model box (the anode is at the top, the cathode at the bottom). Rows: potential, log10 n and log10 p; columns: DEVSIM, network, and network minus DEVSIM (the colour scale of the two density differences is clipped at the 99th percentile). Bottom: cuts along the vertical line through the middle of the anode window. The potential differs by at most 2.9 mV, at the corners of the junction. log10 p differs by up to 1.7 in the last row next to the cathode; over the whole box its 99th percentile is 0.04.
